title: United States and Japan Extend Science and Technology Agreement Indefinitely
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026
Today in Tokyo, the United States and Japan signed a protocol that extends and amends the U.S.-Japan Agreement on Cooperation in Research and Development in Science and Technology, also known as the U.S.-Japan Science and Technology Agreement. Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Michael Kratsios signed for the United States and Minister for Foreign Affairs Motegi Toshimitsu signed for Japan.
First signed in 1988, the Science and Technology Agreement provides a legally binding framework for scientific cooperation between the U.S. and Japanese governments. Under this framework, the United States and Japan have built countless links between their scientific communities.
The protocol extends the Agreement indefinitely, a sign of the deep trust and respect between the U.S. and Japanese governments. The extended and amended Agreement positions both countries to sustain and strengthen their cooperation, with a focus on critical and emerging technologies that improve the lives of both peoples.
The indefinite extension reaffirms the long-term U.S. and Japanese commitment to close partnership on science and technology, while advancing a secure, trusted innovation ecosystem that benefits both nations.

title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Horii
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Readout


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today with Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Iwao Horii, building on the momentum of President Trump’s meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in New York on September 22. The Deputy Secretary and the State Minister recognized the importance of the U.S.-Japan Alliance and their commitment to regional peace and stability. They discussed continued cooperation in the Pacific Islands, including development and infrastructure projects, in support of a free and open Indo-Pacific region. The leaders also reaffirmed their shared commitment to enhancing economic security in other regions of mutual interest.

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: Ad-Hoc Coalition to Defeat ISIS Meeting on Iraq and Syria
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026
Italy hosted, and co-chaired with the United States, an ad-hoc Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS/Daesh meeting of Political Directors and senior diplomatic officials in Rome on October 1, 2026.
Coalition partners congratulated Iraq and Syria on the success of Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR) in degrading ISIS/Daesh. The ending of OIR’s mandate in Iraq represents true victory of the collective efforts of the Coalition and the resolve of the Iraqi government to continue its responsibility to ensure the group cannot regenerate. In Syria, we celebrate the Coalition having a partner in Damascus that recognizes the ISIS/Daesh threat and is determined to work with the Coalition to diminish it. Lasting security in both countries will depend on strengthening inclusive, sovereign state institutions capable of representing and protecting all communities who can equally partake in their country’s future.
Participants reaffirmed the Coalition’s role as a tool for strengthening Iraq and Syria’s stability and that international support should focus on enhancing both countries’ abilities to develop their capacity to target ISIS/Daesh and to prevent the grievances and divisions that ISIS/Daesh has historically exploited. Coalition members expressed their readiness to work closely with the Syrian and Iraqi governments to accomplish this and announced commitments totaling more than 75 million dollars towards supporting Syrian counterterrorism needs, and increasing detention capacity, sustaining health and sanitation services, and supporting displaced and detained populations for both Iraq and Syria.
The Government of Syria highlighted key counterterrorism priorities and gaps for international support and Iraq reaffirmed its ongoing leadership to defeat ISIS/Daesh.

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: Joint Statement on the Anniversary of the Snapback of UN Restrictions on and Related to Iran
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026
The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Albania, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Belize, Bosnia, Bulgaria, Canada, Colombia, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Estonia, Federated States of Micronesia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liberia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Marshall Islands, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Palau, Panama, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, The Netherlands, Trinidad and Tobago, Ukraine, United Kingdom, and Yemen.
Begin Text
On September 27, 2025 (at 8:00 p.m. EDT), six United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs) – 1696 (2006), 1737 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), 1929 (2010) – returned into force pursuant to the completion of the snapback process. France, Germany, and the United Kingdom initiated this process in response to Tehran’s persistent and significant non-performance of its nuclear commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).
One year on, we, the Proliferation Security Initiative (PSI)-endorsing States listed above, affirm our commitment to the continued implementation of all relevant obligations enumerated in the reinstated UNSCRs. We further recall that the 2003 Statement of Interdiction Principles (2003), which all PSI participants have endorsed, affirms our adherence to all relevant international law and frameworks, including the UNSCRs.
We further commit, consistent with our UNSCR obligations, to continue to take measures – consistent with relevant domestic and international authorities and related commitments – to prevent the supply, sale, or transfer to Iran of items, materials, equipment, goods, and technology that could contribute to proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities or the development of nuclear weapon delivery systems, as well as to uphold the restrictions on the supply, sale, or transfer of arms and related materiel to or from Iran.
Our countries further reaffirm our commitment to ensuring sufficient domestic legal authorities and capabilities to address Iran’s proliferation-sensitive activities. More concretely, we commit to (1) undertake effective measures to prevent the direct or indirect sale, supply, and transfer to and from Iran of items from or through their territories that could contribute to weapons of mass destruction, their means of delivery (including UAVs), and related materials and items subject to the reinstated UNs arms restrictions; (2) adopt streamlined procedures to facilitate the rapid exchange between PSI partners of relevant information concerning Iran’s proliferation activities; (3) where needed, continue to keep our national legal authorities under review to ensure the effectiveness of our measures; and (4) take appropriate specific actions in support of interdiction efforts related to Iran’s proliferation activities.
We welcome all national-level efforts to implement our UNSCR obligations, as well as relevant activities that support our objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, such as those linked to Operation Economic Outcast.
We urge all UN Member States to implement these resolutions and reiterate the international community’s longstanding concerns about Iran’s nuclear program. We will continue to coordinate our counterproliferation efforts to counter any attempts by Iran to undertake UNSCR-prohibited efforts to resume development of its nuclear or ballistic missile programs. We call on Iran to return to compliance with its nonproliferation obligations, and cooperate fully with the IAEA, and address the international community’s proliferation concerns.
End Text

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: United States Cuts Off Hamas Financing Network
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026

Today’s designations by the U.S. Department of the Treasury target a Hamas military operative in Gaza and a France-based fundraising network that used sham charities and cryptocurrency to collect nearly $2 million for Hamas in recent years.
This action underscores the enduring U.S. commitment to dismantling Hamas’s global support networks and denying the group the resources it needs to plan and carry out terrorism that threatens the security of Americans, our partners, and the broader Middle East. It reflects close coordination between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the FBI to expose how Hamas exploits humanitarian and charitable structures abroad to disguise terrorist financing as legitimate aid work.
The United States will continue working with partner governments, including France, to identify and hold accountable individuals and organizations that provide Hamas cover to raise and transfer funds internationally. Disrupting these networks is central to broader U.S. efforts to isolate Hamas, protect the integrity of legitimate humanitarian assistance to Gazan civilians, and support conditions for lasting regional stability.
We are committed to ensuring that humanitarian aid can be delivered by reliable and safe organizations that advance legitimate Palestinian interests and lasting peace in the region.
Today’s designations were issued pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, the United States’ core counterterrorism sanctions authority. On October 31, 2001, the U.S. Department of State designated Hamas pursuant to E.O. 13224 for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals, or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States. Hamas is also designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: Guinea National Day
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
October 2, 2026
On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Guinea on the 68th anniversary of your independence.
The United States and Guinea share a growing partnership built on mutual interest and benefit. This year, in partnership with your elected leadership, we deepened cooperation on critical minerals development to strengthen all secure and reliable supply chains. We also launched a new global health security partnership to help Guinea build a sustainable, self-sufficient public health capacity. These achievements reflect our shared commitment to prosperity and security for both our peoples.
I send my best wishes to all Guineans as you celebrate this important day.

title: Joint Statement in Support of Bolivia’s Efforts to Fight Corruption and Narco-Trafficking
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
October 1, 2026
The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, and Trinidad and Tobago.
Begin Text:
The governments participating in the Shield of the Americas commend the Government of Bolivia for its decisive actions to confront narco-trafficking, tackle corruption, and hold enablers accountable. The Shield countries encourage Bolivia’s continued investigation and prosecution of these networks. The recent high-profile law enforcement actions against current and former senior officials implicated in narcotrafficking send a powerful message: Bolivia’s democratically elected government and other Shield countries will no longer tolerate illicit influence in our hemisphere, no matter how high it reaches.
At the historic Shield of Americas leaders meeting on September 22, the 15 countries stood united in our unwavering commitment to defend democratically elected governments and protect regional security against the corrosive influence of narco-terrorist networks.
Today, we stand firmly with Bolivia.
End Text.
